instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Brush a sheet pan with 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Finely grate the Parmesan on the small holes of a box grater until you have about 1/2 cup. In a shallow bowl, mix the Parmesan, panko, oregano, basil, paprika and the other 1 tbsp olive oil.
Pat the tilapia dry with paper towels and lay the fillets on the sheet pan. Sprinkle both sides with the salt, garlic powder and pepper.
Spread about 2 tsp of the mayonnaise over the top of each fillet in a thin, even layer. That should be about 3 tbsp in all.
Press the Parmesan mixture onto the mayonnaise so it forms a thick, even coat.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the topping is golden and the fish flakes when you press a fork into the thickest part.
If the topping isn't golden yet, switch the oven to broil and cook for 1 minute. Watch it closely.
Cut the lemon into wedges and squeeze 1 wedge over the fish.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or another squeeze of lemon.
Serve with the rest of the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Wholesome Yum (the lead) seasons the fillets, spreads a thin layer of mayonnaise on top, covers it with Parmesan and dried herbs and bakes at 400°F for 10 to 12 minutes. Six Sisters' Stuff uses crushed Ritz crackers with Parmesan, a lemon juice dip and a 425°F bake of about 20 minutes. Both say to dry the fish well and bake until it flakes. This one follows the lead, scaled from 6 fillets to 4, and adds panko and a little olive oil to the Parmesan so the crust is crisper.
